_note: Each runway-wind and runway-choice rule's figures and boundaries, written down from the source it cites (the FAA's handbook and chart, AC 90-66C, 14 CFR 91.126, the AIM), never from the code. Shape and checks as engine/facade/tests/common/cases.rs says; asked by engine/facade/tests/rule_cases.rs.

cases.name: Calm is 00000KT
cases.source: AIM 7-1-28, Key to Aerodrome Forecast (TAF) and Aviation Routine Weather Report (METAR): "00000KT - wind calm".

cases.name: 3 kt is not calm
cases.source: AIM 7-1-28, Key to Aerodrome Forecast (TAF) and Aviation Routine Weather Report (METAR): "00000KT - wind calm".

cases.name: No wind reported is not calm
cases.source: AIM 7-1-28, Key to Aerodrome Forecast (TAF) and Aviation Routine Weather Report (METAR): "00000KT - wind calm". A report with no wind group says nothing of calm; taking it for calm would choose runways on nothing (the safer side).

cases.name: A gust's crosswind over the steady one is the one judged
cases.source: Cessna 172S POH (1998) section 4, maximum demonstrated crosswind velocity; 14 CFR 91.103(b): the most crosswind the wind brings, gusts included, is the one held to the airplane's figure, unsigned (the safer side).

cases.name: No gust: the steady crosswind, unsigned
cases.source: As the gust case: the steady crosswind where no gust is reported, from either side.

cases.name: A runway's crosswind is its gust's where more
cases.source: As wind_steady_or_gust, on a runway's own wind.

cases.name: Nothing along or across: calm
cases.source: AIM 7-1-28, Key to Aerodrome Forecast (TAF) and Aviation Routine Weather Report (METAR): "00000KT - wind calm".

cases.name: 1 kt across is not calm
cases.source: AIM 7-1-28, Key to Aerodrome Forecast (TAF) and Aviation Routine Weather Report (METAR): "00000KT - wind calm".

cases.name: Runway 18L at 3 degrees west is 177 true
cases.source: FAA-H-8083-25C ch. 16, magnetic variation: a true heading is the magnetic one with an east variation added and a west one taken off; a runway's number is its magnetic heading in tens of degrees (AIM 2-3-3).

cases.name: Runway 9 at 4 degrees east is 094 true
cases.source: FAA-H-8083-25C ch. 16, magnetic variation: a true heading is the magnetic one with an east variation added and a west one taken off; a runway's number is its magnetic heading in tens of degrees (AIM 2-3-3).

cases.name: A helipad has no runway heading
cases.source: NASR APT_RWY: a helipad's ident (H1) is no runway number; AIM 2-3-3's numbering is a runway's.

cases.name: 300 at 12 on runway 9/27 (088/268 true): 27, 10 kt along, 6 kt from the right
cases.source: FAA-H-8083-25C (Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge), ch. 11, the crosswind component chart: a wind's component along the runway is its speed times the cosine of its angle off the runway, across it the sine (the chart's arcs and lines drawn to those). AC 90-66C (2023) 11.5, Runway Preference: "Landing and takeoff should be accomplished on the operating runway most nearly aligned into the wind."
cases.method: 32 degrees off 268: 12 cos 32 = 10.2, 12 sin 32 = 6.4, the whole knots as the planner writes them; from the right is positive.

cases.name: 040 at 10 gusting 20 on runway 9 (088 true): from the left, 7 and 15 kt across
cases.source: FAA-H-8083-25C (Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge), ch. 11, the crosswind component chart: a wind's component along the runway is its speed times the cosine of its angle off the runway, across it the sine (the chart's arcs and lines drawn to those). AC 90-66C (2023) 11.5, Runway Preference: "Landing and takeoff should be accomplished on the operating runway most nearly aligned into the wind."
cases.method: 48 degrees off 088 from the left: 10 sin 48 = 7.4, 20 sin 48 = 14.9.

cases.name: No report: no runway wind
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.103(b): with no wind reported, no runway is said to be favoured by it.

cases.name: C81 by KUGN's 220 at 8 gusting 15: runway 24, 18 degrees off from the left
cases.source: FAA-H-8083-25C (Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge), ch. 11, the crosswind component chart: a wind's component along the runway is its speed times the cosine of its angle off the runway, across it the sine (the chart's arcs and lines drawn to those). AC 90-66C (2023) 11.5, Runway Preference: "Landing and takeoff should be accomplished on the operating runway most nearly aligned into the wind."
cases.method: 238 true is 18 degrees off 220, 058 is 162 (a tailwind), 088 and 268 are 48 and 132: 24 is the most nearly into the wind.

cases.name: No wind to go by: no pick
cases.source: AC 90-66C 11.5 needs a wind; with none, none is picked by it.

cases.name: The runway flown is the one most nearly into the wind where none is picked
cases.source: AC 90-66C (2023) 11.5, Runway Preference: "Landing and takeoff should be accomplished on the operating runway most nearly aligned into the wind."
cases.method: 27 has 12 kt along it, 36 none and 12 across.

cases.name: The pilot's pick stands
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.3(a): the pilot in command picks the runway; AC 90-66C 11.5 recommends, it does not oblige.

cases.name: A closed runway is never the one flown, picked or not
cases.source: AIM 2-3-6, closed runways (the X): no takeoff or landing on one; AC 90-66C 11.5's "operating runway".

cases.name: The runway in use is the one most nearly into the wind
cases.source: AC 90-66C (2023) 11.5, Runway Preference: "Landing and takeoff should be accomplished on the operating runway most nearly aligned into the wind."

cases.name: Each end left traffic but where the FAA flags it right
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.126(b)(1): "Each pilot of a powered fixed-wing aircraft must make all turns to the left unless the airport displays approved light signals or visual markings indicating that turns should be made to the right"; AIM 4-3-3: right patterns are charted "RP". FAA-H-8083-25C ch. 16, magnetic variation: a true heading is the magnetic one with an east variation added and a west one taken off; a runway's number is its magnetic heading in tens of degrees (AIM 2-3-3).

cases.name: Left traffic on an east heading: the pattern is to the north
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.126(b)(1): "Each pilot of a powered fixed-wing aircraft must make all turns to the left unless the airport displays approved light signals or visual markings indicating that turns should be made to the right"; AIM 4-3-3: right patterns are charted "RP".

cases.name: Right traffic on an east heading: the pattern is to the south
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.126(b)(1): "Each pilot of a powered fixed-wing aircraft must make all turns to the left unless the airport displays approved light signals or visual markings indicating that turns should be made to the right"; AIM 4-3-3: right patterns are charted "RP".

cases.name: No traffic said: left
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.126(b)(1): "Each pilot of a powered fixed-wing aircraft must make all turns to the left unless the airport displays approved light signals or visual markings indicating that turns should be made to the right"; AIM 4-3-3: right patterns are charted "RP".

cases.name: 27015G25KT on runway 27 (270 true), no variable group: none across
cases.source: FMH-1 (Federal Meteorological Handbook No. 1) chapter 12, the wind group, and AIM 7-1-28's METAR key: "dddVddd" reports a direction varying between two bounds, clockwise, where it varies by 60 degrees or more at over 6 knots; the wind may blow from anywhere in between. FAA-H-8083-25C ch. 11, the crosswind component: speed times the sine of the angle off the runway.
cases.method: The wind straight down the runway: sin 0 = 0, steady and gusting.

cases.name: 27015G25KT 230V310 on runway 27: judged at 230, the first bound, 16 kt from the left in the gusts
cases.source: FMH-1 (Federal Meteorological Handbook No. 1) chapter 12, the wind group, and AIM 7-1-28's METAR key: "dddVddd" reports a direction varying between two bounds, clockwise, where it varies by 60 degrees or more at over 6 knots; the wind may blow from anywhere in between. FAA-H-8083-25C ch. 11, the crosswind component: speed times the sine of the angle off the runway.
cases.method: At either bound 40 degrees off: 15 sin 40 = 9.64, 25 sin 40 = 16.07; the end still the mean's, 27; 230 is from the left (negative), the first bound of the two equal worst; the exact crosswind is unsigned.
